cohort: The study included two cohorts, each of 50 pregnant women with regular menstrual cycles, who had reached a gestational age of 40 weeks or more, up to 42 weeks, comparing those in spontaneous labour with those undergoing induced labour.
finding: While no significant differences were found in most maternal and foetal outcomes between spontaneous and induced labour at 40-41 weeks, spontaneous labour at 41-42 weeks was associated with a significantly higher incidence of meconium-stained liquor and a higher rate of LSCS compared to induced labour.
mod_finding: The rate of Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS) was significantly higher in the spontaneous labour group (26%) compared to the induced labour group (10%).
gest_age: 40 weeks or more, up to 42 weeks
